2009 AP Honorable Mention All-American }} '''Eric Maynor''' is an American basketball [[point guard]] for the VCU Rams. He is currently a senior, and averaged 22.4 points, 6.2 assists, 3.6 rebounds and 1.7 steals per game in the [[2008-09 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2008-2009]] season. Maynor is considered a late-lottery or mid-first-round pick in the first round of the 2009 NBA Draft.Radford, Rich. - "This is The Player ODU Must Face Today". - ''[[The Virginian-Pilot]]''. - January 17, 2009. ==College career== ===2008-09=== During the 2008-09 season, Eric Maynor became VCU's all-time leader in assists[http://vcuathletics.tv/mbb/0809results/mbb-gameday.php] and made free-throws[http://vcuathletics.tv/mbb/0809results/mbb-gameday.php]. On February 28th, Eric Maynor became the leading scorer in VCU history with a floater against Georgia State. As of March 10th, 2009, he had scored a school record 1,929 points. Eric also lead VCU to a second CAA title during his career, scoring 25 points in a 71-50 victory over George Mason on March 9th, 2009 at the [[Richmond Coliseum]]. The Rams went on to the [[2009 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2009 NCAA Tournament]] but lost to [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] when Maynor missed a buzzer-beater to win the game. ===2007-08=== Maynor helped VCU win the [[Colonial Athletic Association|CAA]] regular season title, though the team fell in the semi-finals of the conference tournament to [[William & Mary Tribe men's basketball|William & Mary]]. He was selected as the CAA Player of the Year and selected to the All-CAA first team.[http://www.caasports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=43048&SPID=3455&DB_OEM_ID=8500&ATCLID=1406497 Maynor is CAA Player of the Year] The Rams failed to reach the NCAA Tournament and went on to play in the NIT, where they lost in the first round against UAB. ===2006-07=== On [[March 15]], [[2007]], Maynor scored 22 points, including the game winning shot, in VCU's victory over [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] in the first round of the [[2007 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament]]. This shot, popularized by the CBS call, has been known as the Duke Dagger. Maynor's last minute heroics are also what helped VCU to overcome [[George Mason Patriots men's basketball|George Mason]] in the 2007 [[Colonial Athletic Association|CAA]] championship game. Over the 2007 summer, Maynor was also selected to represent the United States in the [[Pan American Games]]. Played alongside DJ White and Michael Beasley. Maynor was also named one of the top 25 preseason candidates for the Men’s 2007-08 [[John R. Wooden Award]], the nation’s most prestigious college basketball honor. ==High school career== As a senior led Westover High School team to a North Carolina state championship scoring 25 points on March 14, 2005. http://collegebasketball.rivals.com/content.asp?cid=398511. ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== [http://www.vcuathletics.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=62451&SPID=6846&DB_OEM_ID=14500&ATCLID=813821&Q_SEASON=2007 Player page on VCUathletics.com] {{CAA Men’s Basketball POY}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Maynor, Eric}} [[Category:1987 births]] [[Category:American basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from North Carolina]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:People from Fayetteville, North Carolina]] [[Category:Point guards]] [[Category:Virginia Commonwealth Rams men's basketball players]] {{US-hoops-bio-stub}}
